## Architecture

The statistics live in one engine in `R/`, shared by the Shiny app, the R interface and the exported code:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `utils.R` | small shared helpers (formatting, labels, `%||%`) |
| `provenance.R` | disappR and package versions, optional packages, runtime state |
| `simulation.R` | teaching simulations with known answers |
| `import.R` | file reading, the bundled empirical examples |
| `validation.R` | data integrity checks |
| `data-preparation.R` | column mapping, standardisation, individual metrics, model data |
| `formulas.R` | Models 1-10, covariate and built terms, random-effect structures |
| `model-fit.R` | fitting one model and the model suite, validity classification |
| `model-comparison.R` | AIC tables, likelihood-ratio tests, family comparison, accuracy against simulated truth |
| `diagnostics.R` | residual and model checks |
| `trajectories.R` | population predictions, observed means, individual fits |
| `disappearance.R` | decomposition and the selective disappearance/appearance diagnostics |
| `missingness.R` | sampling and missingness diagnostics |
| `interpretation.R` | interpretation notes built from the fitted results |
| `ui-helpers.R` | help texts and interface helpers used by the app |
| `export.R` | reproducible R code and reports |
| `api.R` | the R interface (below) |
| `run_app.R` | `run_app()` |

`inst/app/global.R` only loads packages, sets options and loads this engine, and `server.R` only orchestrates: it reads
inputs, calls the engine, stores results and renders outputs. The engine was moved out of `global.R` (0.9.10) and the
pure helpers out of `server.R` (0.9.11) verbatim, so every result is the same as in 0.9.9.

Every model comparison stores its provenance (`disappr_provenance(fit)`): a fingerprint of the analysed rows and
individuals, formulas, family, random effects, transformations, settings, warnings and software versions. Saved
results and reports include it, and so does the header of the exported script. The exported script runs the same
engine as the app when the same disappR version is installed, and otherwise a standalone reconstruction with lme4 /
glmmTMB.

Scripted analyses use the same functions as the app:

```r
x   <- disappr_prepare(my_data, disappr_mapping(id = "ID", age = "age", trait = "mass", life = "lifespan"))
fit <- disappr_fit(x, models = c("M1", "M2", "M4"), age_function = "Quadratic", family = "gaussian")
disappr_compare(fit); disappr_diagnose(fit); disappr_interpret(fit)
disappr_predict(fit, "M4")
disappr_provenance(fit)
ex <- disappr_example("bouwhuis")            # bundled data, mapping and settings
cat(disappr_code(fit, x, "my_data.csv"))
```

To deploy the app where the package is not installed (for example shinyapps.io), `source("inst/scripts/bundle_app.R")`
writes a self-contained `disappR_app/` folder with the engine included.

## Tests (please run these first)

`tests/scripts/run_all.R` runs seven tiers; tier 7 (`sweep_0_20.R`) covers the changes made in 0.20.9 to 0.20.19: the Trajectories page with sparse individuals and count traits, the clamping of extreme curves, duplicates and multi-group IDs, per-model row sets, the evidence summary across Models 1-10, the likelihood-ratio pairs, and every bundled example. Set `DISAPPR_SWEEP_FULL=1` to fit models for all of them.


```sh
Rscript tests/scripts/smoke_test.R   # every analysis function on simulated data + the fly-data replication
Rscript tests/scripts/app_test.R     # drives the real server with shiny::testServer() and renders every output
```

Both scripts collect problems instead of stopping, and finish with a `FAILURES` / `Output problems` block.

## Testing

Unit tests (testthat, in `tests/testthat/`) run with R CMD check or `testthat::test_local()`. `Rscript tests/scripts/run_all.R`
runs every tier in order: unit, smoke, golden regression (with `DISAPPR_GOLDEN_REF`), robustness
(adversarial, metamorphic, lme4 oracle, exported-code equivalence), app server, stress, and empirical/simulation checks.
`Rscript tests/scripts/release_gate.R` adds R CMD check and requires the golden comparison against the previous release.

`tests/golden/` checks that a version reproduces another exactly (formulas, analysed rows, coefficients,
log-likelihoods, AIC, predictions, validity, notes, decomposition, observed means and exported code) for all ten
examples and eight simulated designs. To confirm this version against 0.9.9 on your machine:

```
Rscript tests/golden/golden_capture.R /path/to/disappR_0.9.9 golden_0.9.9.rds
Rscript tests/golden/golden_capture.R .                      golden_0.9.10.rds
Rscript tests/golden/golden_compare.R golden_0.9.9.rds golden_0.9.10.rds
```

`tests/scripts/robustness_suite.R` is an optional check, not part of the app: it runs metamorphic invariants, a comparison with
hand-written lme4 fits, an exported-code round trip in a fresh R session, adversarial data and reactive-state tests
(`Rscript tests/scripts/robustness_suite.R` from the package root; `DISAPPR_BIG=1` adds large-data timings).

From the package root:

```r
Rscript tests/scripts/smoke_test.R    # every analysis function on simulated data and the fruit-fly reanalysis
Rscript tests/scripts/app_test.R      # the Shiny server with shiny::testServer()
Rscript tests/scripts/stress_test.R   # 26 realistic, adversarial and simulated datasets, 6,000-individual timings
```

Each script ends with a list of expectations (PASS / CHECK) and any FAILURES.

Continuous integration (`.github/workflows/`) runs R CMD check on Linux, Windows and macOS and the full test tiers on
every push and pull request.

## Step 4 runs in its own process

With the `callr` package installed, the individual fits on the Trajectories page run in a separate R process: an error, a hang or a crash there ends only that process, and a job running longer than three minutes is stopped. Without `callr` they run in the app's process and the page says so.

## Reproducible versions

Numbers can shift slightly between versions of lme4, glmmTMB and their optimisers. To record the versions behind
published results, run from the package root:

```r
source("inst/scripts/lock_dependencies.R")
```

It writes `dependency_versions.csv` (R and every package disappR uses) and, if the renv package is installed,
`renv.lock`, which `renv::restore()` can reinstall elsewhere. Exported model scripts also start with the versions
used by the app session. The Start page lists which optional packages are installed and what each one adds.
